clue.text: A country still on the gold standard, apparently?

definitions.text: A country still on the gold standard, apparently?

parts.words: A country still on the gold standard, apparently?
parts.note: a self-governing nation is read whimsically as one whose state is still run on the gold coin of old British currency

explanation.surface: A question about a nation that has kept its currency tied to gold.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign was an old British gold coin, so the clue pictures a nation still paying its way in sovereigns.
explanation.definitionFit: An independent nation that governs itself is the standard political term for a fully self-ruling country.

clue.text: Dubious character

definitions.meaning: a person thought guilty, as police call a likely culprit

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means doubtful or questionable; as a noun it is a person under suspicion, a shady character.

clue.text: Much better description of what the Jumbo Jet was in aviation development

definitions.meaning: greatly improved, a big step up

definitions.text: description of what the Jumbo Jet was in aviation development
definitions.meaning: the huge Boeing 747 was literally an enormous leap forward in aircraft design

explanation.surface: A remark that the Jumbo Jet marked a huge leap forward in aviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A great step up is something markedly better; the 747 was also physically huge, so the phrase fits it doubly.

clue.text: What kept the artist at home?

definitions.text: What kept the artist at home?

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A question about what stopped a painter going out.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole, bad weather is what keeps a painter indoors; as wordplay, RA (artist) is followed by IN (at home).
explanation.definitionFit: Wet weather is the classic reason an outdoor painter stays indoors.

clue.text: A case of frigidity

parts.note: read literally, a container holding coldness, i.e. a chest packed with frozen water to keep food chilled

explanation.surface: A diagnosis of someone with a cold, unresponsive nature.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a medical or psychological case; read literally it is a box of ice.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned cooler or refrigerator is literally a chest filled with frozen water.

clue.text: Country people girded at swimming

indicators.note: girded means encircled, so the country's people wrap around the next word

parts.note: a nation is a country's people

explanation.surface: A nation's citizens lined up for a swimming event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country people' is the misleading phrase: it suggests rural folk, but it gives a whole nation; 'girded' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the formal Latin-derived word for the sport and act of swimming.

clue.text: It tells us when a distribution of mail gets in

indicators.note: distribution suggests the letters of the following words being dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: Something tells us the moment the post arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a distribution of' rearranges MAILGETSIN; the surface's postal sense of distribution is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast pip or bleep marking the exact hour tells listeners what o'clock it is.

clue.text: Of course, it can tumble men at that bend

definitions.text: Of course, it can tumble men at that bend

parts.words: Of course, it can tumble men at that bend
parts.note: on a racecourse there is a famous sharp downhill turn where jockeys are often thrown from their horses

explanation.surface: A warning that riders may come off at a tricky turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' means 'on the racecourse': this is the famous downhill bend on Epsom Downs, the English course where the Derby is run.
explanation.definitionFit: This turn on the Epsom racecourse is notorious for falls, so riders do tumble there.

clue.text: Good health? Career sportsmen need it

parts.note: professionals, pros for short, are career sportsmen

explanation.surface: A toast, then a remark that professional athletes need to stay fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A German and Latin drinking toast meaning 'may it benefit you', said like 'cheers'.

clue.text: Famous old chapel is set in order anew

indicators.note: to put in order anew is to rearrange, so the letters before it are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Instructions to rearrange the furnishings of a historic chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican chapel whose ceiling Michelangelo painted is among the most famous in the world.

clue.text: One who makes a bad offer seem attractive

definitions.text: One who makes a bad offer seem attractive

parts.words: One who makes a bad offer seem attractive
parts.note: someone who lures another into wrongdoing by making it look appealing, like the devil

explanation.surface: A description of a salesman pushing a poor deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a slick salesman; the deeper sense is the Devil enticing someone to sin.
explanation.definitionFit: One who entices others to sin, such as Satan, presents wrongdoing as appealing.

clue.text: Live round that's no good

indicators.note: turned round, so the word before is read backwards

explanation.surface: Live ammunition is dangerous, no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reverses LIVE; the surface reads it as a live round of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness is the opposite of goodness, so the wicked are no good.

clue.text: Pretty poor linesmen?

parts.note: linesmen are taken as writers of lines of verse, and pretty poor ones at that

explanation.surface: A jibe at incompetent football or tennis officials.
explanation.walkthrough: Linesmen suggests sports officials, but here they are versifiers who write poor lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferior or would-be poets who write bad verse are mocked with this term.

clue.text: The wonderful charm of a character like Circe

definitions.text: The wonderful charm of a character like Circe

parts.words: The wonderful charm of a character like Circe
parts.note: Circe, the enchantress of Homer's Odyssey, turned men to swine with sorcery; her charm is an incantation

explanation.surface: Praise for the allure of a seductive mythical woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Charm looks like personal attraction; here it is an enchantment cast by a sorceress.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchantment or incantation such as a sorceress like Circe would cast.

clue.text: Work that goes out for formal occasions?

definitions.text: Work that goes out for formal occasions?

indicators.note: the word that goes on the outside, wrapping around the work

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Something worn when going out to formal events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes out' means THAT goes outside OP; the whole clue also describes headwear donned for smart events.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall silk hat is traditional formal wear for weddings and Ascot.

clue.text: Wild guess made with a telescope lens, perhaps

definitions.meaning: an attempt with little chance of success

definitions.text: made with a telescope lens, perhaps
definitions.meaning: a photograph taken from far away

explanation.definitionFit: An outside chance is a guess unlikely to come off; a distant photograph taken with a telephoto lens fits literally.

clue.text: Cattle not raised on the banks of the Tees

definitions.text: on the banks of the Tees

parts.note: livestock, stock for short, includes cattle

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means turned upward, so the word is read bottom to top

explanation.surface: Livestock not being reared beside a northern English river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses NOT to TON. The town is Stockton-on-Tees in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The full name of this north-east English town includes on-Tees, as it stands beside that river.

clue.text: Big bang experts who believe in fragmentation

definitions.meaning: followers of the ancient theory that matter consists of indivisible particles

explanation.definitionFit: Physicists working on nuclear fission make big bangs; philosophers like Democritus held all matter to be tiny indivisible units.

clue.text: One act reviewed without delay

indicators.note: re-viewed, looked at again in a new arrangement, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A one-act play gets reviewed quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediately, straight away, means doing something with no delay.

clue.text: French city packed with marines for the opera

indicators.note: packed with means filled, so the city holds the other part inside it

parts.note: Caen is a city in Normandy

explanation.surface: A Normandy city full of servicemen for an opera performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Caen is in Normandy; 'packed with' signals the container, and 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizet's famous opera about a Spanish gypsy cigarette girl bears this name.

clue.text: Establishment of growing importance for playful toddlers

definitions.meaning: a place where plants are grown and sold
a room or school where small children play

explanation.definitionFit: A garden centre raising young plants, and also a playroom or preschool for small children.

clue.text: Cunningly steer round a difficult problem

indicators.note: goes round, so the shuffled letters surround the next piece
done cunningly, the letters are craftily rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to steer carefully around a tricky obstacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cunningly' rearranges STEER into TESER, and 'round' puts it around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain-teaser is a puzzle or tricky question.

clue.text: Everybody knows it starts with the dismemberment of Crete

parts.note: opens is a synonym of starts, as in a show opening

indicators.note: dismembering pulls the word apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A story of a well-known affair beginning with Crete being carved up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' looks like a verb of beginning in the surface, and it is: it supplies a synonym, while 'the dismemberment of' scrambles the island's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something meant to be private but in fact known to everyone.

clue.text: Obstinately determined to see the sights of Mesopotamia?

parts.note: to do a place is to tour it, as in 'doing Paris'
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Someone resolute about sightseeing in ancient Iraq.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'do' a place is to tour its sights; Ur, home of Abraham, stands for Mesopotamia.
explanation.definitionFit: Grim and stern, unyieldingly firm in manner.

clue.text: A high speed piece of film

definitions.meaning: a fast pace, as in 'going at a ...'
a short extract from a movie

explanation.definitionFit: A brisk pace is a rapid rate; a short excerpt is cut from a longer film.

clue.text: But Henry VIII didn't find him so ready to forgive!

definitions.text: But Henry VIII didn't find him so ready to forgive!

parts.words: But Henry VIII didn't find him so ready to forgive!
parts.note: the pope who refused the king's annulment from Catherine of Aragon shares his name with a word for merciful

explanation.surface: A remark that the Tudor king found someone unforgiving.
explanation.walkthrough: Pope Clement VII refused to annul Henry VIII's first marriage, so to Henry he was anything but merciful.
explanation.definitionFit: Merciful or lenient; the pope who blocked Henry's divorce bore it as his papal name.

clue.text: Shakespearean justice observed in Trappist monastery

definitions.meaning: Justice Shallow's companion, a country magistrate in Henry IV Part 2
Trappist monks keep a rule of not speaking

explanation.definitionFit: A rustic magistrate in Henry IV Part 2 bears the name; Trappist monks keep a vow of quiet.

clue.text: Ill-gotten gains?

parts.note: goods acquired dishonestly, such as loot taken by a thief

explanation.definitionFit: Loot obtained through theft is the literal case of possessions gained wrongly.
